solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marsh deer, say

parts.note: the musk deer is a small Asian deer, so deer can stand for musk
say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: A deer seen out on boggy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marsh' looks like a describing word for the deer, but it is the definition; the deer is a musk deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A muskeg is a North American bog of sphagnum moss, a kind of wetland.

clue.text: Club price is steep

parts.note: a mace is a heavy club used as a weapon
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: A golf club's fees are steep.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it in liquid, which is what macerating does.

clue.text: Before burnng bridges, put up picture

indicators.note: before places the reversed bridges ahead of the word for burning
in a down clue, put up means the word for bridges is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: spans are bridges or arches
burning, as misprinted here, means hot

explanation.surface: Someone about to burn their bridges puts up a photograph first.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held misprints 'burning' as 'burnng'; it means HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph, a kind of picture.

clue.text: She turns up in several legends

indicators.note: turns up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heroine keeps appearing in many old tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the letters lie inside 'several legends'; 'turns up' reads them upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a woman's first name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Nancy's Mum needs money in advance for expensive fabric

indicators.note: in advance puts the money first, ahead of the mother

parts.note: cash is money
Nancy is a French city, so a mum from there is a French mère

explanation.surface: A girl's mother has to pay up front for a luxurious material.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a girl's name but is the city in France, so its mum speaks French: MERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine, costly wool from Kashmir goats, a luxury textile.

clue.text: A punter can purchase vacuous fashion accessory

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reshaped
vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters of purchase are left

explanation.surface: A shopper can buy a trendy, mindless clothing extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' empties 'purchase' to PE; that joins A PUNTER CAN and 'fashion' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An appurtenance is an accessory or adjunct that goes with something larger.

clue.text: Basil Brush at last meets royal? Bravo!

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word brush

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher
Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Basil Brush, the puppet fox, meets a royal and is cheered.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil Brush is a British children's TV puppet fox; here Basil is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a culinary herb, so the herb is defined by an example.

clue.text: Catch business associate coming up short

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up reads the letters from the bottom upwards
short means missing its last letter

parts.note: a partner is an associate in a business

explanation.surface: A work colleague can be caught out arriving without enough money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts PARTNER to PARTNE, and 'coming up' turns that over.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap is to catch someone in a trap or by trickery.

clue.text: I'll enter plea, not wanting second bit of jury duty

indicators.note: enter means the letter I goes into the word for plea, replacing another

parts.note: an excuse is a plea in defence

indicators.note: not wanting removes the second letter of the word jury

parts.note: I'll gives the letter I, the speaker

explanation.surface: Someone plans to plead to escape jury service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll enter' puts I into EXCUSE in place of U, the second letter of 'jury'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excise is a tax levied on goods, a duty in the customs sense.

clue.text: The first to decide Clare is off her rocker?

indicators.note: off as in going off, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
the first to picks the opening letter of decide

explanation.surface: The first to decide that Clare is crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off her rocker' means mad, but the definition is just 'rocker': D and CLARE are reshuffled by 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a baby's bed that rocks, so it is a rocker.

clue.text: Viewer takes a long time giving description of Lulu?

indicators.note: takes means the word for viewer holds the time period inside

parts.note: optic is an eye or lens, something to view with
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A TV viewer takes ages explaining a pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Lulu looks like the Scottish pop singer, but it is Alban Berg's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Berg's Lulu is an opera, so operatic is a fitting adjective for it.

clue.text: Peter remains with core of personnel — employment's not threatened at all

parts.note: peter is old slang for a safe
ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: core of picks the middle letter of personnel

parts.note: employment is uses, as in its uses

explanation.surface: Peter's job remains secure, with the staff assured.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is old criminal slang for a safe; 'employment's' is read as 'employment is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely secure, with no risk at all.

clue.text: A deception fraudster used regularly

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter, here the even ones of fraudster; the same letters also run across fraudster used, a coincidence since no word signals concealment

explanation.surface: A swindler's habitual trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse is a trick or stratagem meant to deceive.

clue.text: Run into rebel activist group

indicators.note: into puts the letter for run inside the rebel's name

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rebel joins a militant band.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade was the leader of a 1450 Kentish revolt against Henry VI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained activists in a party or movement.

clue.text: See 17
After half a pill he attains oblivion

indicators.note: after places the pronoun following the half pill
half keeps one half of the word for pill, here the back half

parts.note: a tablet is a pill

explanation.surface: Once he has taken half a pill, a man passes out.
explanation.walkthrough: TABLET halved gives LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth, so it stands for oblivion.

clue.text: One that's planted in crowd's picked up on the mike

indicators.note: a microphone picks up sound, so the word for crowds is heard, not spelt

parts.note: flocks are crowds, read as the plural

explanation.surface: Someone in a crowd is overheard on a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlox is a garden flowering plant, so it is something that gets planted.

clue.text: How Doris and Robin may be remembered? Ah, happy times!

definitions.text: How Doris and Robin may be remembered?
definitions.meaning: Doris Day the US singer and Robin Day the British broadcaster are both remembered as ...
the wistful phrase recalls the good old times

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Day was a famous British TV political interviewer; Doris Day was an American film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a nostalgic sigh for good times now gone, also a 1968 hit song.

clue.text: Smear's written about head of industry in column

indicators.note: written about means the word for smear goes around the other letter

parts.note: to plaster is to smear thickly

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of industry

explanation.surface: Daubing is reported about a captain of industry in a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smear's written about' reads as 'smear is written around'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilaster is a flat rectangular column set into a wall.

clue.text: To her, see, exercising is what keeps loafer in shape

indicators.note: exercising works the letters around into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling a woman exercise keeps a lazy person fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loafer' suggests an idler, but it is a slip-on shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoetree is a shaped insert that keeps a shoe's form when not worn.

clue.text: Composer Khachaturian's first five so-Soviet works repelling European?

indicators.note: this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order
first five keeps the opening five letters of the name Khachaturian
repelling means the European is driven out of the word Soviet

explanation.surface: Asks whether a composer's first five works were so Soviet that they repelled Europeans.
explanation.walkthrough: KHACH, SO and SOVIT (Soviet without E) are rearranged by 'works'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dmitri Shostakovich was a major Soviet composer of symphonies.

clue.text: Can it close completely?

definitions.meaning: can it is slang for stop talking
to fasten or seal something entirely, as with a house or shop

explanation.definitionFit: Shut up is both a rude order to be quiet and a way of saying closed fully.

clue.text: Agent will be fine with Guinness, say

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
Sir Alec Guinness was an actor

explanation.surface: An agent will be happy with a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness looks like the stout but is the actor Alec Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an agent who buys and sells on another's behalf.

clue.text: Husband gets one involved in neat trick

indicators.note: involved in places the letter for one inside the word for neat

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
a is one

explanation.surface: A husband gets caught up in a clever piece of trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is an archaic word for cattle, so OX.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax is a trick played to deceive people.

clue.text: A painter? Utter nonsense!

indicators.note: utter means speak, so the word for nonsense is said aloud

parts.note: bosh is nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the claim that a person is an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter of fantastic scenes.

clue.text: Daughter's a mischief-maker, see

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: Look, the girl is a little troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and folly.
explanation.definitionFit: To date someone is to see them romantically.

clue.text: Initially lost temper, pursuing origin of Friar Tuck

indicators.note: pursuing puts the trimmed temper after the friar's letter
origin of picks the first letter of friar
initially lost drops the first letter from the word for temper

parts.note: a mood is a temper, as in being in a mood

explanation.surface: Friar Tuck, of Robin Hood's band, loses his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for food, as in a tuck shop; Friar Tuck is in Robin Hood stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British slang for snacks or food, especially at school.

clue.text: American guy carries little weight — he's a bit dim

indicators.note: carries means the word for guy holds the weight inside

parts.note: bo is American slang for a man or pal
oz, the ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: An American who carries little weight is rather stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bozo is American slang for a stupid person or fool.

clue.text: One can fly out — times will vary

indicators.note: will vary means the letters change into another order

explanation.surface: A person may get out, though the times change.
explanation.definitionFit: A titmouse is a small bird, so it is one that can fly.

clue.text: Ponder about end of Nat King Cole

indicators.note: about means the word for ponder wraps round the letter

parts.note: to pore over something is to ponder it

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of Nat

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Thinking about the end of the singer Nat King Cole.
explanation.walkthrough: Nat King Cole points to the singer, but the definition is 'Cole', for the songwriter Cole Porter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter was the American songwriter, so his surname goes with Cole.

clue.text: One makes fun of standard poet

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
an odist is a poet who writes odes

explanation.surface: Someone mocks an ordinary poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist imitates others' work to mock it.

clue.text: Husky's an animal to pull vehicle around Arctic, chiefly

indicators.note: around means the animal's name goes round the letter

parts.note: a horse is an animal that pulls a cart

indicators.note: chiefly takes the first letter of Arctic

explanation.surface: A husky is a dog to pull a sled across the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky looks like the sled dog of the surface, but means a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, which is what hoarse means.
